chunks: And as for what Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who performed three circuits or fewer of the tawaf, then saw blood. He said: She retains her place; when she becomes pure, she performs the tawaf and counts what has passed. The correct interpretation of this report is that we understand it as referring to the tawaf of the voluntary (nafl) prayer, because we have clarified that it is permissible to build upon it even if it is less than half. And similarly for the man when he becomes junub, his ruling is the same as the menstruating woman's, on equal footing.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who starts menstruating during the tawaf if she has performed fewer than four circuits?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the ruling for a woman whose *tawaf* is interrupted by menstruation, establishing that she retains her place and completes the remaining circuits upon purification. Shaykh al-Tusi contextualizes this by interpreting the report as referring to *tawaf al-nafilah* (voluntary circumambulation), where performing fewer than four circuits is permissible, thereby distinguishing it from the stricter requirements of *tawaf al-ada* (obligatory). This highlights the Shia juristic principle of flexibility in ritual completeness when interrupted by natural biological states.
